_readme: The scene manifest. One record per beat. Design fields (id, time, act, spectacle, camera, setPiece, len) are read by the set pieces; content fields (kicker, title, body, tags, staged, log and the per-beat extras under 'copy') are read by the captions. Rewriting copy never moves a scene. Every time is staged.

beats.title: You go home.
beats.body: For four years, one engineer has been quietly building an entire company out of agents. They are hired, seated and reviewed. They have directors and managers, a mailroom, a clock on the wall and a records room that forgets nothing. And the company has been at work the whole time.

copy.secondary: Watch one meeting go through it

log.subject: bloodbank.cli.session.ended
log.note: You go home. The company doesn't.

interlude.line: Four bylaws. Everything else follows from them.

beats.title: Every agent is an employee.
beats.body: Stop asking how to orchestrate a swarm. Ask how a company would handle it. Companies already solved delegation, escalation, onboarding, record-keeping and who to call when something breaks. Map every problem to the workplace and the ceiling goes away.

copy.quote: “Anthropomorphism as protocol: employees, titles, desks, records. Never ‘fleet’.”
copy.quoteSource: From the charter of FLUME, the workforce

beats.title: Nothing calls. Everything announces.
beats.body: No component knows who is listening. Every hook, decision, ticket and spoken sentence becomes an event on one bus, and whoever cares picks it up. Hire a new department and nobody else has to change their job.

listeners.name: HOLOCENE

beats.title: Built from scratch, on purpose.
beats.body: Almost every part of 33GOD was written for it, to one strict set of rules: layered abstraction, one owner for every building block, extension over rewrites, reuse over copies. So each new component plugs in instead of rewiring the rest.

copy.note: Lower layers never call higher ones. Every block has one owner.

log.subject: bloodbank.agent.tool.completed
log.note: Built from scratch, on purpose. Five layers; calls only travel downhill.

beats.title: The company runs on itself.
beats.body: For its whole life, 33GOD has run every project its builder touches, itself included. Every rough edge becomes a ticket. The ticket finds the manager who owns the fix. The fix ships back into the thing that found it. Four years of that, every day.

log.subject: bloodbank.task.cycle.reviewed
log.note: The company runs on itself. The loop closes on its own board.

interlude.sub: Everybody has transcripts now. Here is what happens after.

beats.kicker: Everybody has this. It is where most people stop.
beats.title: Your transcript is waiting when you leave the room.
beats.body: Long recordings like this one go to Wax, HeyMa's long-form transcriber. It is done before you have found your next meeting.

log.subject: bloodbank.audio.file.received
log.note: The recording lands.

log.subject: bloodbank.audio.transcription.completed
log.note: Your transcript is waiting when you leave the room.

beats.title: Then it reads itself.
beats.body: Enrichment passes comb the transcript and find every project it touched. The calls are made by Jev, Typesafe's System One model, built for one job: quick, typed, yes-or-no judgments.

log.subject: bloodbank.evt.conversation.turn.annotated
log.note: Then it reads itself. Jev finds every project the meeting touched.

beats.kicker: Four people, one desk, one microphone.
beats.title: No Zoom? No problem. Speakers still get labeled.
beats.body: All diarization is backed by a custom-built voice-fingerprint service, so people are told apart by their voices, not by which laptop they dialed in from. The room is the meeting.

log.subject: bloodbank.project.activity.recorded
log.note: Speakers get labeled by voice, not by laptop.

beats.kicker: There is no “teach it a word” button. There does not need to be.
beats.title: It learns your vocabulary. Nobody asked it to.
beats.body: Project names, people and jargon join a self-evolving dictionary as they are spoken, and Jev decides what earns a place. Nothing is configured. It works because everything is connected.

log.subject: bloodbank.repo.decision.recorded
log.note: New words join the dictionary. Nobody asked it to.

beats.kicker: Action items do not go into a doc to die.
beats.title: When the meeting ends, the harvest begins.
beats.body: Decisions and commitments become tickets through Pilot, a custom ticket-provider abstraction over Plane, Linear and Trello. Each ticket already knows which board it belongs to.

log.subject: bloodbank.task.ticket.created
log.note: When the meeting ends, the harvest begins. Four tickets.

beats.title: Each ticket walks itself to its project manager.
beats.body: The PM owns the ticket's whole life. It plans the work, picks the next move, hands it to the right employee and closes the loop. Underneath, Krebs runs that lifecycle the same way on every board.

log.subject: bloodbank.task.ticket.assigned
log.note: Each ticket walks itself to its project manager.

beats.kicker: This is the part that sounds made up.
beats.title: Then the managers talk to each other.
beats.body: When one PM finds a fix another project could use, it takes the liberty of telling that project's manager. Across projects, unprompted.

copy.message: PM → PM · a fix you can use

beats.body: Skills are declared in manifests and compose like parts. One catalog fans out to every agent CLI, so a new skill reaches every employee at once.

interlude.line: And then it starts to read like fiction.

beats.kicker: F-01 · Day one of every project
beats.title: PJangler. The project factory.
beats.body: A project registry and bootstrapper. Every project is built from a vetted pipeline template, so on day one it already has a ticket board, a git repo, its own project manager and its own Open Notebook. A mobile app gets one more hire: a Launch Director, who works with Google and Apple to see it through a smooth launch.

beats.title: HeyMa. Transcription, translation and telephony, on any stack.
beats.body: A full-featured audio pipeline that runs on any platform, next to whatever you already use. On its own, it is the most flexible, full-featured audio pipeline you can run today. Inside 33GOD it fits so well that you forget it is there. It just works.

parts.name: SHORTWAVE
parts.line: Turns your phone into a walkie-talkie that drives every open terminal, from anywhere.

transcript._readme: Staged words for Act III. Marked spans: {p:…} a project Jev finds, {w:…} a word the dictionary learns. 'ticket' is the index of the ticket a line becomes.

lines.text: Okay. {p:Holocene} first. The {w:stuck-work panel} still shows tickets that closed yesterday.
That's the {w:lifecycle lag}. I'll take it. Fixed by Thursday.
While we're in there, {p:HeyMa} dropped the last minute of Tuesday's call.
Then somebody decide the {p:Shortwave} pairing flow.
Decision: pair by QR, no codes. I'll write it up.
Last thing. {p:Candybar} owns the {w:nightly digest} now, not a cron.

tickets.title: Fix the lifecycle lag on the stuck-work panel
Recover the last minute of Tuesday's call
Move the nightly digest onto the clock
